passage.text: When people think of great inventions, they usually think of America or Japan.
passage.reading: wɛn ˈpiːpəl ˈθɪŋk əv ˈɡreɪt ɪnˈvɛnʃənz, ðeɪ ˈjuːʒuəli ˈθɪŋk əv əˈmɛrɪkə ɔːr dʒəˈpæn.

passage.text: But some useful inventions come from Thailand, too.
passage.reading: bʌt sʌm ˈjuːsfəl ɪnˈvɛnʃənz ˈkʌm frəm ˈtaɪlænd, ˈtuː.

passage.text: The energy drink Krating Daeng was first made in Thailand in 1976.
passage.reading: ði ˈɛnərdʒi ˌdrɪŋk krəˈtɪŋ ˈdɛŋ wʌz ˈfɜːrst ˈmeɪd ɪn ˈtaɪlænd ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈsɛvənti ˈsɪks.

passage.text: It was made for drivers and other people who worked long hours.
passage.reading: ɪt wʌz ˈmeɪd fər ˈdraɪvərz ənd ˈʌðər ˈpiːpəl huː ˈwɜːrkt ˈlɔːŋ ˈaʊərz.

passage.text: Later, a businessman from Austria changed the recipe a little and sold it around the world as Red Bull.
passage.reading: ˈleɪtər, ə ˈbɪznəsmæn frəm ˈɔːstriə ˈtʃeɪndʒd ðə ˈrɛsəpi ə ˈlɪtəl ənd ˈsoʊld ɪt əˈraʊnd ðə ˈwɜːrld əz ˈrɛd ˈbʊl.

passage.text: Sriracha sauce is Thai, too. Its name comes from Si Racha, a town by the sea.
passage.reading: sɪˈrɑːtʃə ˈsɔːs ɪz ˈtaɪ, ˈtuː. ɪts ˈneɪm ˈkʌmz frəm ˈsiː ˈrɑːtʃə, ə ˈtaʊn baɪ ðə ˈsiː.

passage.text: Other Thai inventions are solutions to big problems.
passage.reading: ˈʌðər ˈtaɪ ɪnˈvɛnʃənz ər səˈluːʃənz tə ˈbɪɡ ˈprɑːbləmz.

passage.text: King Bhumibol had the idea of artificial rain for farmers in the 1950s, and the first tests were done in 1969.
passage.reading: ˈkɪŋ ˈpuːmɪpɔːn ˈhæd ði aɪˈdiːə əv ˌɑːrtɪˈfɪʃəl ˈreɪn fər ˈfɑːrmərz ɪn ðə ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈfɪftiz, ənd ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈtɛsts wɜːr ˈdʌn ɪn ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈsɪksti ˈnaɪn.

passage.text: Planes put chemicals into clouds, and the clouds produce rain.
passage.reading: ˈpleɪnz ˈpʊt ˈkɛmɪkəlz ˈɪntuː ˈklaʊdz, ənd ðə ˈklaʊdz prəˈduːs ˈreɪn.

passage.text: He also designed a machine that cleans dirty water by adding air to it.
passage.reading: hiː ˈɔːlsoʊ dɪˈzaɪnd ə məˈʃiːn ðæt ˈkliːnz ˈdɜːrti ˈwɔːtər baɪ ˈædɪŋ ˈɛr tu ɪt.

passage.text: Today, these ideas still help farmers and cities all over Thailand.
passage.reading: təˈdeɪ, ˈðiːz aɪˈdiːəz ˈstɪl ˈhɛlp ˈfɑːrmərz ənd ˈsɪtiz ˈɔːl ˈoʊvər ˈtaɪlænd.

passage.text: Finally, pad thai is an invention, too!
passage.reading: ˈfaɪnəli, ˈpɑːd ˈtaɪ ɪz ən ɪnˈvɛnʃən, ˈtuː!

passage.text: It became popular in the 1940s, when the government wanted people to eat more noodles.
passage.reading: ɪt bɪˈkeɪm ˈpɑːpjələr ɪn ðə ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈfɔːrtiz, wɛn ðə ˈɡʌvərnmənt ˈwɑːntɪd ˈpiːpəl tu ˈiːt ˈmɔːr ˈnuːdəlz.

passage.text: Now it is a global favorite.
passage.reading: ˈnaʊ ɪt ɪz ə ˈɡloʊbəl ˈfeɪvərɪt.
